answer.line: A round trip is there and back: 23 + 23 = 46 km.

steps: Read the words before the numbers. Round trip means there and back: two legs of 23 km.
Double it in pieces: 20 x 2 = 40 and 3 x 2 = 6, so 40 + 6 = 46 km.
Check the size: each leg is a little over 20 km, so the round trip is a little over 40 and under 50. 46 fits.

choices.note: 36 is ten short of 46, a slip in the adding with no rule behind it. 40 + 6 = 46.
40 doubles the 20 and leaves out 3 x 2. Add the 6: 46.
56 is ten past 46, a phantom carry. 23 + 23 needs no carry at all.
146 adds a hundred that is not there. Two legs of 23 km stay under 50.

lockIt: Round trip means there and back: double the one-way distance.

playWith.label: Mental Math Tricks: type 23 x 2 and use Distribute to split it into 20 and 3

visual.alt: Top bar: two 23 km legs end to end, there and back. The bottom bar, the same length and outlined, is the 46 km round trip. A dashed mark at 40 shows where doubling only the tens stops.
visual.caption: Lay the two legs end to end: the round trip bar matches them exactly.
